findings.text: String parameter support exposes install, render and release operations joined in a single operations table. Install replaces the stored pointer with a copy or borrowed reference, render emits stored text with trailing newline, release drops the stored allocation.

Boolean parameter family exposes plain, enable-only, inverted and integer-storing variants. Plain treats absent value as true and delegates parsing, enable-only permits only transitions toward true, inverted stores complement, integer variant stores parsed truth as integer. Each variant publishes an operations table, most marked as accepting no separate argument.

Array and fixed-string parameters expose set, render and release operations. Array handling parses comma separated elements through per-element callbacks with cardinality bounds, renders by joining per-element outputs with commas, and releases each element when element release exists. Fixed-string handling copies into caller storage with capacity check.

Module parameter sysfs lifecycle exposes setup, removal and destruction helpers. Setup publishes each visible parameter under the owning module, removal withdraws the group and frees bookkeeping, destruction invokes per-parameter release callbacks without touching sysfs.

Identifier lookup helpers expose reference-taking translation from numbers or pid objects to task structures, numeric translation within a namespace, and iteration to next allocated identifier. One helper also resolves pid file descriptors including self thread and self thread-group selectors.

Identifier mutation helpers expose reassignment of associations, exchange of thread identifiers between two tasks, transfer of linkage from one task to another, and deferred release through a callback. Mutation helpers require exclusive ownership of the global task list.

String install rejects inputs longer than about one thousand characters with a no-space error and reports out-of-memory when allocation fails. When early-boot allocation is unavailable it borrows the caller pointer instead of copying, otherwise it stores a private duplicate and releases the prior value.

Absent boolean value behaves as true. Enable-only install first parses into scratch storage, rejects attempts to move from true to false with a read-only-filesystem error, and only writes through when the new value is true. Inverted variant stores logical negation and swaps rendered letters.

Array install enforces minimum and maximum cardinality, reporting invalid argument when exceeding maximum or falling below minimum. Each element advances the destination by fixed stride and increments the count, using temporary count storage when no shared counter is supplied. Rendering joins element outputs with comma separators and terminates output explicitly.

Fixed-string install measures input length against descriptor capacity and rejects overlong input with no-space error before copying including terminator. Parameters with zero permission are treated as invisible and skipped during both modular setup and builtin enumeration.

Initial pid object starts with reference count one, three empty task associations, level zero and a single numeric entry zero bound to the initial namespace. Initial namespace starts in adding state, level zero, with idle reaper and initial user namespace and default maximum. Minimum and maximum bounds derive from reserved count plus one and global limit.

Pidfd open rejects flags outside nonblock and thread selectors and rejects non-positive identifiers with invalid argument, reports missing target as no-such-process, and drops its temporary reference after creating the descriptor. Pidfd task resolution reports missing task as no-such-process and returns file flags through an out parameter.

Parameter sysfs show and store paths serialize against concurrent updates by acquiring the owning module parameter lock before invoking the type-specific callback and releasing afterward. Array element callbacks are preceded by a locked-state check.

Thread identifier exchange and linkage transfer require the global task list to be held for writing, asserted at entry. Exchange swaps list heads and per-task pointers with ordering-safe primitives plus cached numeric values.

Identifier-to-task translations and numeric queries execute under read-side critical sections entered and exited around the lookup, taking an extra task reference before exit when returning a task. A dedicated cache-aligned spinlock guards identifier allocation maps.

Sysfs parameter bookkeeping pairs a module attribute with a constant parameter descriptor. A container holds a count, an attribute group and a counted flexible array of those pairs, with a separate null-terminated pointer array shadowing the pairs for group publication.

Each parameter type publishes a constant operations table linking set, render and optional release handlers plus flags where applicable. Boolean family shares a common renderer, inverted has its own renderer, integer-storing bool reuses integer renderer, array links its three static handlers.

Static pid and namespace objects encode reference state, task association lists, nesting level, numeric entries and namespace linkage. Namespace includes common linkage, identifier allocator, allocation state, level, reaper pointer, user namespace link, maximum value and conditional noexec scope.

Module sysfs dispatch uses an operations table mapping show and store to module attribute handlers, a uevent filter accepting only module objects, a uevent operations table, a global kset pointer, a release handler completing an optional completion, and a type object joining release and operations.

Pid namespace sysctl support defines a root with lookup, permission and ownership handlers plus a single entry describing the maximum identifier. The entry points at the initial namespace maximum, carries integer length, permissive mode and min-max handler with pointers to global bounds.

Parameter group publication starts empty on first use with a parameters group name and single null slot, then grows both the container and pointer array by one per addition, zeroes the new slot, initializes its attribute, links descriptor and handlers, fixes all shadow pointers and re-terminates with null.

Module sysfs object handling first attempts lookup by name and returns on hit. On miss it allocates, tags ownership, initializes and adds the object, optionally creates a uevent file, handles failure with release and diagnostic, and takes an extra reference so both paths return with a held reference. Callers later remove old groups before re-adding, create the group with fatal assertion on failure at boot, emit addition event and drop their reference.

Builtin enumeration walks the linker-delimited parameter range, skips invisible entries, splits names at the first dot to derive module versus core ownership and name offset, then delegates to per-module addition. Version enumeration walks its own range and publishes one file per entry with one-time warning on failure. Initialization creates the module set first, then requires it before running version and parameter enumeration in order.

Pidfd creation prepares a file object and on success installs it under a new descriptor number, returning that number. Opening looks up the numeric target with a temporary reference, delegates to creation, then drops the temporary reference.

System call entry for opening a process descriptor accepts a numeric identifier and flag word, validates them, translates the identifier to an internal object, creates a descriptor and returns its number or a negative error.

Sysfs show and store entries for modules resolve the generic attribute and object to typed structures, reject missing type-specific handlers with input-output error, and delegate to those handlers. Parameter-specific show and store add permission and safety checks plus locking around type callbacks. Version show renders the stored version with newline.

String install in early boot without allocator borrows caller memory rather than copying, so lifetime depends on caller preservation. Array install temporarily overwrites each separator in the caller buffer with a terminator during parsing, requiring writable input and restoring traversal via saved separator.

Show without a render handler and store without an install handler fail cleanly. Store additionally consults an unsafe predicate under lock and fails with permission error when disallowed. Writability of the sysfs file is decided once at creation from any write bit in the declared mode, so later permission changes cannot enable storing.

Adding an invisible parameter, failing to add or create groups during boot, and transferring the primary thread identifier type are treated as programming errors with fatal or one-time-warning diagnostics. Modular setup and group creation failures trigger immediate cleanup of partially built bookkeeping.

String rendering and version rendering bound output by page size and append newline. Boolean rendering uses uppercase Y for true and N for false, inverted swaps them. Parameter group name, module set name and core module pseudo-name are fixed strings. Array wrapper enforces minimum one.

Maximum identifier sysctl entry uses mode giving read-write to owner and read to others, integer length, and min-max enforcement with global lower and upper objects. Lower equals reserved count plus one, upper equals global limit, initial value equals default.

Overlong string inputs report no-space, allocation failures report out-of-memory, array bound violations report invalid argument, forbidden boolean clear reports read-only filesystem, missing handlers or disallowed stores report permission error, missing attribute handlers report input-output error, unknown pid targets report no-such-process, flag or identifier validation failures report invalid argument, set creation failures report out-of-memory.
